questions.text: Let $\mathrm{S}=\{x^3+ax^2+bx+c: a, b, c\in\mathbb{N}$ and $a, b, c\le20\}$ be a set of polynomials. Then the number of polynomials in S, which are divisible by $x^2+2$, is
questions.sol:
$x^3+ax^2+bx+c=(x^2+2)(x+k)=x^3+kx^2+2x+2k$.
So $b=2$, $a=k$, $c=2a$, with $2a\le20$: $a=1,\ldots,10$, i.e. 10 polynomials.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If $\alpha$, $\beta$, where $\alpha<\beta$, are the roots of the equation $\lambda x^2-(\lambda+3)x+3=0$ such that $\dfrac1\alpha-\dfrac1\beta=\dfrac13$, then the sum of all possible values of $\lambda$ is
questions.sol:
$\lambda x^2-(\lambda+3)x+3=(\lambda x-3)(x-1)$, so the roots are $1$ and $3/\lambda$.
If $3/\lambda>1$: $1-\dfrac\lambda3=\dfrac13$, $\lambda=2$ (valid).
If $3/\lambda<1$: $\dfrac\lambda3-1=\dfrac13$, $\lambda=4$ (valid).
Sum $=6$.

questions.text: Let $z$ be a complex number such that $|z-6|=5$ and $|z+2-6i|=5$. Then the value of $z^3+3z^2-15z+141$ is equal to
questions.sol:
The circles have centres $(6,0)$ and $(-2,6)$, both of radius 5; the centres are 10 apart, so the circles touch at the midpoint: $z=2+3i$.
$z^2=-5+12i$, $z^3=-46+9i$.
$z^3+3z^2-15z+141=(-46-15-30+141)+(9+36-45)i=50$.

questions.text: Let A, B and C be three $2\times2$ matrices with real entries such that $\mathrm{B}=(\mathrm{I}+\mathrm{A})^{-1}$ and $\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{I}$. If $\mathrm{BC}=\begin{bmatrix}1&-5\\-1&2\end{bmatrix}$ and $\mathrm{CB}\begin{bmatrix}x_1\\x_2\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}12\\-6\end{bmatrix}$, then $x_1+x_2$ is
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{I}-\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}=(\mathrm{I}+\mathrm{A})^{-1}$ are both functions of A, so they commute: $\mathrm{CB}=\mathrm{BC}$.
$x_1-5x_2=12$ and $-x_1+2x_2=-6$ give $x_2=-2$, $x_1=2$.
$x_1+x_2=0$.

questions.text: The common difference of the A.P.: $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_m$ is 13 more than the common difference of the A.P.: $b_1, b_2, \ldots, b_n$. If $b_{31}=-277$, $b_{43}=-385$ and $a_{78}=327$, then $a_1$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Common difference of the $b$'s: $\dfrac{-385+277}{12}=-9$, so that of the $a$'s is $4$.
$a_1=327-77\times4=19$.

questions.text: A bag contains 10 balls out of which $k$ are red and $(10-k)$ are black, where $0\le k\le10$. If three balls are drawn at random without replacement and all of them are found to be black, then the probability that the bag contains 1 red and 9 black balls is:
questions.sol:
Take the 11 values of $k$ as equally likely. $P(\text{3 black}\mid k)=\binom{10-k}{3}\big/\binom{10}{3}$.
By Bayes' theorem the required probability is $\dfrac{\binom93}{\sum_{m=0}^{10}\binom m3}=\dfrac{84}{\binom{11}{4}}=\dfrac{84}{330}=\dfrac{14}{55}$.

questions.text: The mean and variance of 10 observations are 9 and 34.2, respectively. If 8 of these observations are 2, 3, 5, 10, 11, 13, 15, 21, then the mean deviation about the median of all the 10 observations is
questions.sol:
Sum $=90$, and the eight given values add to 80, so the other two add to 10.
Sum of squares $=10(34.2+81)=1152$; the eight give 1094, so the other two give 58. Hence they are 3 and 7.
Ordered data: 2, 3, 3, 5, 7, 10, 11, 13, 15, 21; median $=8.5$.
Sum of $|x_i-8.5|=50$, so the mean deviation is $5$.

questions.text: Let $\mathrm{S}=\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9\}$. Let $x$ be the number of 9-digit numbers formed using the digits of the set S such that only one digit is repeated and it is repeated exactly twice. Let $y$ be the number of 9-digit numbers formed using the digits of the set S such that only two digits are repeated and each of these is repeated exactly twice. Then,
questions.sol:
$x$: choose the repeated digit (9 ways) and 7 of the other 8 digits (8 ways); arrangements $9!/2!$. So $x=36\cdot9!$.
$y$: choose the two repeated digits $\binom92=36$ and 5 of the other 7 digits $\binom75=21$; arrangements $9!/(2!2!)$. So $y=189\cdot9!$.
$x/y=36/189=4/21$, i.e. $21x=4y$.

questions.text: Let ABC be an equilateral triangle with orthocenter at the origin and the side BC on the line $x+2\sqrt2\,y=4$. If the co-ordinates of the vertex A are $(\alpha, \beta)$, then the greatest integer less than or equal to $\left|\alpha+\sqrt2\beta\right|$ is
questions.sol:
In an equilateral triangle the orthocentre is also the centroid, so A lies on the normal to BC through O, on the other side, at twice the distance of BC from O.
Foot of the perpendicular from O to BC: $\dfrac{4}{9}(1,2\sqrt2)$. So $\mathrm{A}=-\dfrac89(1,2\sqrt2)$.
$\alpha+\sqrt2\beta=-\dfrac89-\dfrac{32}{9}=-\dfrac{40}{9}$; $\left\lfloor\dfrac{40}{9}\right\rfloor=4$.

questions.text: Let $y=x$ be the equation of a chord of the circle $\mathrm{C_1}$ (in the closed half-plane $x\ge0$) of diameter 10 passing through the origin. Let $\mathrm{C_2}$ be another circle described on the given chord as its diameter. If the equation of the chord of the circle $\mathrm{C_2}$, which passes through the point $(2, 3)$ and is farthest from the center of $\mathrm{C_2}$, is $x+ay+b=0$, then $a-b$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{C_1}$ lies in $x\ge0$ and passes through O with diameter 10, so it touches the y-axis at O: $x^2+y^2-10x=0$. The chord $y=x$ meets it at $(5,5)$.
$\mathrm{C_2}$ has centre $(2.5, 2.5)$. The chord through $(2,3)$ farthest from the centre is perpendicular to the line joining the centre to $(2,3)$, whose direction is $(-1,1)$.
Chord: $-x+y=1$, i.e. $x-y+1=0$, so $a=-1$, $b=1$ and $a-b=-2$.

questions.text: If $\dfrac{\tan(\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B})}{\tan\mathrm{A}}+\dfrac{\sin^2\mathrm{C}}{\sin^2\mathrm{A}}=1$, $\mathrm{A, B, C}\in\left(0,\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, then
options: tan A, tan B, tan C are in G.P.
tan A, tan B, tan C are in A.P.
tan A, tan C, tan B are in G.P.
tan A, tan C, tan B are in A.P.
questions.sol:
$1-\dfrac{\tan(A-B)}{\tan A}=\dfrac{\sin B}{\sin A\cos(A-B)}$, so the condition is $\dfrac{\sin A\sin B}{\cos(A-B)}=\sin^2C$.
Dividing by $\cos A\cos B$: $\dfrac{\tan A\tan B}{1+\tan A\tan B}=\dfrac{\tan^2C}{1+\tan^2C}$, hence $\tan A\tan B=\tan^2C$.
So tan A, tan C, tan B are in G.P.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If the distances of the point $(1, 2, a)$ from the line $\dfrac{x-1}{1}=\dfrac{y}{2}=\dfrac{z-1}{1}$ along the lines $\mathrm{L_1}:\dfrac{x-1}{3}=\dfrac{y-2}{4}=\dfrac{z-a}{b}$ and $\mathrm{L_2}:\dfrac{x-1}{1}=\dfrac{y-2}{4}=\dfrac{z-a}{c}$ are equal, then $a+b+c$ is equal to
questions.sol:
A point of the given line is $(1+t,2t,1+t)$.
Along $\mathrm{L_1}$: $(1+3s,2+4s,a+bs)$. Then $t=3s$ and $2+4s=6s$, so $s=1$, $t=3$ and $a+b=4$. Distance $=\sqrt{25+b^2}$.
Along $\mathrm{L_2}$: $(1+u,2+4u,a+cu)$. Then $t=u$ and $2+4u=2u$, so $u=-1$ and $a-c=0$. Distance $=\sqrt{17+c^2}$.
Equal distances: $c^2-b^2=8$, i.e. $a^2-(4-a)^2=8$, so $a=3$, $b=1$, $c=3$ and $a+b+c=7$.

questions.text: For three unit vectors $\vec a,\vec b,\vec c$ satisfying $\left|\vec a-\vec b\right|^2+\left|\vec b-\vec c\right|^2+\left|\vec c-\vec a\right|^2=9$ and $\left|2\vec a+k\vec b+k\vec c\right|=3$, the positive value of k is
questions.sol:
The sum of squares is $6-2(\vec a\cdot\vec b+\vec b\cdot\vec c+\vec c\cdot\vec a)=9$, so $\sum\vec a\cdot\vec b=-\tfrac32$.
Then $|\vec a+\vec b+\vec c|^2=3+2\left(-\tfrac32\right)=0$, so $\vec b+\vec c=-\vec a$.
$|2\vec a-k\vec a|=|2-k|=3$, giving the positive value $k=5$.

questions.text: The value of $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}(-1)^{k+1}\left(\dfrac{k(k+1)}{k!}\right)$ is
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{k(k+1)}{k!}=\dfrac{k+1}{(k-1)!}$. With $j=k-1$ the sum is $\displaystyle\sum_{j\ge0}(-1)^j\dfrac{j+2}{j!}=\sum_{j\ge1}\dfrac{(-1)^j}{(j-1)!}+2\sum_{j\ge0}\dfrac{(-1)^j}{j!}$.
$=-e^{-1}+2e^{-1}=\dfrac1e$.

questions.text: The area of the region $\mathrm{R}=\{(x, y): xy\le 8,\ 1\le y\le x^2,\ x\ge 0\}$ is
questions.sol:
For a given $y\ge1$, $x$ runs from $\sqrt y$ to $8/y$; this needs $y^{3/2}\le8$, i.e. $y\le4$.
Area $=\displaystyle\int_1^4\left(\dfrac8y-\sqrt y\right)dy=8\ln4-\dfrac23(8-1)=16\ln2-\dfrac{14}{3}=\dfrac23(24\ln2-7)$.

questions.text: The value of $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\dfrac{\log_e\left(\sec(ex)\cdot\sec\left(e^2x\right)\cdot\ldots\cdot\sec\left(e^{10}x\right)\right)}{e^2-e^{2\cos x}}$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$\ln\sec\theta\approx\theta^2/2$, so the numerator $\approx\dfrac{x^2}{2}\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{10}e^{2k}=\dfrac{x^2}{2}\cdot\dfrac{e^2(e^{20}-1)}{e^2-1}$.
Denominator $=e^2\left(1-e^{2\cos x-2}\right)\approx e^2(2-2\cos x)\approx e^2x^2$.
Limit $=\dfrac{e^{20}-1}{2(e^2-1)}$.

questions.text: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $x\dfrac{dy}{dx}-\sin 2y=x^3\left(2-x^3\right)\cos^2 y$, $x\ne0$. If $y(2)=0$, then $\tan(y(1))$ is equal to
questions.sol:
Divide by $\cos^2y$ and put $t=\tan y$: $x\dfrac{dt}{dx}-2t=2x^3-x^6$, i.e. $\dfrac{dt}{dx}-\dfrac{2t}{x}=2x^2-x^5$.
Integrating factor $1/x^2$: $\dfrac{t}{x^2}=2x-\dfrac{x^4}{4}+C$. $y(2)=0$ gives $C=0$.
At $x=1$: $t=2-\tfrac14=\tfrac74$.

questions.text: If $\displaystyle\int\left(\dfrac{1-5\cos^2x}{\sin^5x\cos^2x}\right)dx=f(x)+\mathrm{C}$, where C is the constant of integration, then $f\left(\dfrac\pi6\right)-f\left(\dfrac\pi4\right)$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sin^4x\cos x}\right)=-\dfrac{4}{\sin^5x}+\dfrac{1}{\sin^3x\cos^2x}=\dfrac{\sin^2x-4\cos^2x}{\sin^5x\cos^2x}=\dfrac{1-5\cos^2x}{\sin^5x\cos^2x}$.
So $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{\sin^4x\cos x}$: $f(\pi/6)=\dfrac{32}{\sqrt3}$, $f(\pi/4)=4\sqrt2$.
Difference $=\dfrac{32-4\sqrt6}{\sqrt3}=\dfrac{4}{\sqrt3}\left(8-\sqrt6\right)$.

questions.text: In a G.P., if the product of the first three terms is 27 and the set of all possible values for the sum of its first three terms is $\mathbb{R}-(a, b)$, then $a^2+b^2$ is equal to _______.
questions.sol:
The middle term is 3, so the sum is $3\left(r+1+\dfrac1r\right)$.
$r+\dfrac1r\ge2$ for $r>0$ and $\le-2$ for $r<0$, so the sum is $\ge9$ or $\le-3$: the set is $\mathbb{R}-(-3,9)$.
$a^2+b^2=9+81=90$.

questions.text: If $k=\tan\left(\dfrac\pi4+\dfrac12\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac23\right)\right)+\tan\left(\dfrac12\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac23\right)\right)$, then the number of solutions of the equation $\sin^{-1}(kx-1)=\sin^{-1}x-\cos^{-1}x$ is _________
questions.sol:
With $\cos\theta=\tfrac23$: $\tan\left(\tfrac\pi4+\tfrac\theta2\right)=\sec\theta+\tan\theta=\tfrac32+\tfrac{\sqrt5}{2}$.
With $\sin\phi=\tfrac23$: $\tan\tfrac\phi2=\dfrac{\sin\phi}{1+\cos\phi}=\dfrac{2}{3+\sqrt5}=\tfrac32-\tfrac{\sqrt5}{2}$. So $k=3$.
RHS $=2\sin^{-1}x-\tfrac\pi2$ must lie in $[-\tfrac\pi2,\tfrac\pi2]$, so $0\le x\le1$. Taking sine: $3x-1=-\cos(2\sin^{-1}x)=2x^2-1$, so $x=0$ or $x=\tfrac32$.
Only $x=0$ is valid (both sides equal $-\tfrac\pi2$): 1 solution.

questions.text: Let PQR be a triangle such that $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{PQ}}=-2\hat i-\hat j+2\hat k$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{PR}}=a\hat i+b\hat j-4\hat k$, $a, b\in\mathbb{Z}$. Let S be the point on QR, which is equidistant from the lines PQ and PR. If $\left|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{PR}}\right|=9$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{PS}}=\hat i-7\hat j+2\hat k$, then the value of $3a-4b$ is _____
questions.note: Dropped in the official final key: full marks to everyone. As printed, the given PS does not lie on QR, so the data are inconsistent.
questions.sol:
S on QR equidistant from PQ and PR means PS bisects angle QPR, so PS is along $\dfrac{\overrightarrow{\mathrm{PQ}}}{3}+\dfrac{\overrightarrow{\mathrm{PR}}}{9}\propto(a-6,\ b-3,\ 2)$.
Matching the direction $(1,-7,2)$: $a=7$, $b=-4$, and $|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{PR}}|=\sqrt{49+16+16}=9$ checks. Then $3a-4b=37$.
However, the bisector meets QR at the point dividing it $1:3$, which gives $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{PS}}=\tfrac14(3\overrightarrow{\mathrm{PQ}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{PR}})=\tfrac14\hat i-\tfrac74\hat j+\tfrac12\hat k$, not the vector printed; the data are inconsistent as stated.

questions.text: The value of $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{20}\left(\left|\sqrt{\pi\left(\int_0^r x\left|\sin\pi x\right|dx\right)}\right|\right)$ is________
questions.sol:
On $[n,n+1]$, put $x=n+t$: $\displaystyle\int_0^1(n+t)\sin\pi t\,dt=\dfrac{2n}{\pi}+\dfrac1\pi=\dfrac{2n+1}{\pi}$.
So $\displaystyle\int_0^r x|\sin\pi x|\,dx=\dfrac1\pi\sum_{n=0}^{r-1}(2n+1)=\dfrac{r^2}{\pi}$, and the term is $\sqrt{r^2}=r$.
Sum $=1+2+\cdots+20=210$.

questions.text: For some $\theta\in\left(0,\dfrac\pi2\right)$, let the eccentricity and the length of the latus rectum of the hyperbola $x^2-y^2\sec^2\theta=8$ be $e_1$ and $l_1$, respectively, and let the eccentricity and the length of the latus rectum of the ellipse $x^2\sec^2\theta+y^2=6$ be $e_2$ and $l_2$, respectively. If $e_1^2=e_2^2\left(\sec^2\theta+1\right)$, then $\left(\dfrac{l_1l_2}{e_1e_2}\right)\tan^2\theta$ is equal to ______
questions.sol:
Hyperbola: $\dfrac{x^2}{8}-\dfrac{y^2}{8\cos^2\theta}=1$, $e_1^2=1+\cos^2\theta$, $l_1=\dfrac{2\cdot8\cos^2\theta}{2\sqrt2}=4\sqrt2\cos^2\theta$.
Ellipse: $\dfrac{x^2}{6\cos^2\theta}+\dfrac{y^2}{6}=1$ (major axis along y), $e_2^2=\sin^2\theta$, $l_2=\dfrac{12\cos^2\theta}{\sqrt6}=2\sqrt6\cos^2\theta$.
Condition: $1+\cos^2\theta=\tan^2\theta+\sin^2\theta$, so $2\cos^2\theta=\tan^2\theta$, giving $\cos^2\theta=\tfrac12$, $\theta=\pi/4$.
Then $l_1=2\sqrt2$, $l_2=\sqrt6$, $e_1e_2=\sqrt{3/2}\cdot\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}=\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$, and the value is $\dfrac{4\sqrt3}{\sqrt3/2}\cdot1=8$.

questions.text:
When both jaws of vernier callipers touch each other, zero mark of the vernier scale is right to zero mark of main scale, $4^{\text{th}}$ mark on vernier scale coincides with certain mark on the main scale. While measuring the length of a cylinder, observer observes 15 divisions on main scale and $5^{\text{th}}$ division of vernier scale coincides with a main scale division. Measured length of cylinder is _________mm.
(Least count of Vernier calliper = 0.1 mm)
questions.sol:
Vernier zero to the right of the main-scale zero means a positive zero error: $+4\times0.1=+0.4$ mm.
Observed reading $=15+5\times0.1=15.5$ mm.
Corrected length $=15.5-0.4=15.1$ mm.

questions.text: In the potentiometer, when the cell in the secondary circuit is shunted with $4\ \Omega$ resistance, the balance is obtained at the length 120 cm of wire. Now when the same cell is shunted with $12\ \Omega$ resistance, the balance is shifted to a length of 180 cm. The internal resistance of cell is _______$\Omega$
questions.sol:
The balance length is proportional to the terminal voltage $\dfrac{ER}{R+r}$.
$\dfrac{180}{120}=\dfrac{12/(12+r)}{4/(4+r)}=\dfrac{3(4+r)}{12+r}$, so $1.5(12+r)=12+3r$ and $r=4\ \Omega$.

questions.text: A particle of mass $m$ falls from rest through a resistive medium having resistive force, $F=-kv$, where $v$ is the velocity of the particle and $k$ is a constant. Which of the following graphs represents velocity $(v)$ versus time $(t)$?
questions.sol:
$m\dfrac{dv}{dt}=mg-kv$ with $v(0)=0$ gives $v=\dfrac{mg}{k}\left(1-e^{-kt/m}\right)$.
The velocity starts at zero, rises with decreasing slope and approaches the terminal value $mg/k$: graph (2).

questions.text:
A block of mass 5 kg is moving on an inclined plane which makes an angle of $30^\circ$ with the horizontal. Friction coefficient between the block and inclined plane surface is $\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$. The force to be applied on the block so that the block will move down without acceleration is _______N.
$(g=10\ \mathrm{m/s^2})$.
questions.sol:
Component of weight down the plane: $mg\sin30^\circ=25$ N.
Kinetic friction (up the plane while moving down): $\mu mg\cos30^\circ=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\cdot50\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}=37.5$ N.
For zero acceleration a push of $37.5-25=12.5$ N down the plane is needed.

questions.text:
Water drops fall from a tap on the floor, 5 m below, at regular intervals of time, the first drop strikes the floor when the sixth drop begins to fall. The height at which the fourth drop will be from ground, at the instant when the first drop strikes the ground is _________m.
$(g=10\ \mathrm{m/s^2})$
questions.sol:
Time to fall 5 m: $5=\tfrac12(10)t^2$, $t=1$ s. Five intervals fit in this time, so each is 0.2 s.
The fourth drop has been falling for $0.4$ s: distance $=\tfrac12(10)(0.4)^2=0.8$ m.
Height above the ground $=5-0.8=4.2$ m.

questions.text:
Two circular discs of radius each 10 cm are joined at their centres by a rod of length 30 cm and mass 600 gm as shown in figure.
If the mass of each disc is 600 gm and applied torque between two discs is $43\times10^5$ dyne.cm, the angular acceleration of the discs about the given axis $AB$ is_______rad/s$^2$.
questions.sol:
The axis AB is perpendicular to the rod, 10 cm from one disc centre and 20 cm from the other, and lies along a diameter direction of each disc.
Discs: $I=\tfrac14MR^2+Md^2$: $15000+60000$ and $15000+240000$ g cm$^2$.
Rod: centre 5 cm from AB: $\tfrac{1}{12}(600)(30^2)+600(5^2)=60000$ g cm$^2$.
Total $I=3.9\times10^5$ g cm$^2$, so $\alpha=\dfrac{43\times10^5}{3.9\times10^5}\approx11$ rad/s$^2$.

questions.text: Two wires $A$ and $B$ made of different materials of lengths 6.0 cm and 5.4 cm, respectively and area of cross sections $3.0\times10^{-5}\ \mathrm{m^2}$ and $4.5\times10^{-5}\ \mathrm{m^2}$, respectively are stretched by the same magnitude under a given load. The ratio of the Young's modulus of $A$ to that of $B$ is $x:3$. The value of $x$ is______.
questions.sol:
$Y=\dfrac{FL}{A\,\Delta L}$; with the same $F$ and $\Delta L$, $Y\propto\dfrac LA$.
$\dfrac{Y_A}{Y_B}=\dfrac{6.0/3.0}{5.4/4.5}=\dfrac{2}{1.2}=\dfrac53$, so $x=5$.

questions.text:
10 kg of ice at $-10\ ^\circ$C is added to 100 kg of water to lower its temperature from $25\ ^\circ$C. Consider no heat exchange to surroundings. The decrement to the temperature of water is __________$^\circ$C.
(specific heat of ice = 2100 J/Kg.$^\circ$C, specific heat of water = 4200 J/Kg.$^\circ$C, latent heat of fusion of ice = $3.36\times10^5$ J/Kg)
questions.sol:
Heat to bring the ice to $0\ ^\circ$C and melt it: $10(2100)(10)+10(3.36\times10^5)=3.57\times10^6$ J (less than the $1.05\times10^7$ J the water can give up, so all the ice melts).
Final temperature $T$: $100(4200)(25-T)=3.57\times10^6+10(4200)T$, so $462000\,T=6.93\times10^6$ and $T=15\ ^\circ$C.
Fall in temperature of the water $=25-15=10\ ^\circ$C.

questions.text: In the following $p$-$V$ diagram the equation of state along the curved path is given by $(V-2)^2=4ap$ where $a$ is a constant. The total work done in the closed path is
questions.sol:
At A and C ($V=1$ and $3$), $p=\dfrac{1}{4a}$. The cycle goes A to B to C along the curve and back along the top line, i.e. anticlockwise, so the net work is negative.
Enclosed area $=\displaystyle\int_1^3\left(\dfrac{1}{4a}-\dfrac{(V-2)^2}{4a}\right)dV=\dfrac{1}{4a}\left(2-\dfrac23\right)=\dfrac{1}{3a}$.
Work $=-\dfrac{1}{3a}$.

questions.text: Which of the following best represents the temperature versus heat supplied graph for water, in the range of $-20\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $120\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ ?
questions.sol:
Heating ice from $-20\ ^\circ$C: the temperature rises to $0\ ^\circ$C, stays constant while the ice melts, rises to $100\ ^\circ$C, stays constant while the water boils, then rises again as steam is heated.
Only graph (1) shows exactly these two horizontal steps, at $0\ ^\circ$C and $100\ ^\circ$C. Graph (2) has no steps, (3) has no melting step, and (4) has an extra step.

questions.text: For the two cells having same EMF $E$ and internal resistance $r$, the current passing through the external resistor $6\ \Omega$ is same when both the cells are connected either in parallel or in series. The value of internal resistance $r$ is ________$\Omega$.
questions.sol:
Series: $I=\dfrac{2E}{6+2r}$. Parallel: $I=\dfrac{E}{6+r/2}$.
Equal currents: $2\left(6+\dfrac r2\right)=6+2r$, i.e. $12+r=6+2r$, so $r=6\ \Omega$.

questions.text: The electric current in the circuit is given as $i=i_0(t/T)$. The r.m.s current for the period $t=0$ to $t=T$ is_______.
questions.sol:
$i_{\text{rms}}^2=\dfrac1T\displaystyle\int_0^T i_0^2\dfrac{t^2}{T^2}\,dt=\dfrac{i_0^2}{3}$.
$i_{\text{rms}}=\dfrac{i_0}{\sqrt3}$.

questions.text:
Three long straight wires carrying current are arranged mutually parallel as shown in the figure. The force experienced by 15 cm length of wire $Q$ is________.
$(\mu_0=4\pi\times10^{-7}\ \mathrm{T.m/A})$
questions.sol:
Force per unit length $=\dfrac{\mu_0I_1I_2}{2\pi d}$.
P (3 A, up) and Q (1 A, down) carry opposite currents and repel: $\dfrac{2\times10^{-7}\cdot3\cdot1}{0.03}=2\times10^{-5}$ N/m, pushing Q towards R.
Q and R (2 A, down) carry parallel currents and attract: $\dfrac{2\times10^{-7}\cdot1\cdot2}{0.02}=2\times10^{-5}$ N/m, also towards R.
Force on 0.15 m $=4\times10^{-5}\times0.15=6\times10^{-6}$ N towards R.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Two point charges of 1 nC and 2 nC are placed at the two corners of equilateral triangle of side 3 cm. The work done in bringing a charge of 3 nC from infinity to the third corner of the triangle is _____ $\mu$J.
$\dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}=9\times10^9\ \mathrm{N.m^2/C^2}$
questions.sol:
Potential at the third corner: $V=\dfrac{9\times10^9\,(1+2)\times10^{-9}}{0.03}=900$ V.
$W=qV=3\times10^{-9}\times900=2.7\times10^{-6}$ J $=2.7\ \mu$J.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
The electric field of an electromagnetic wave travelling through a medium is given by $\vec E(x,t)=25\sin\left(2.0\times10^{15}t-10^7x\right)\hat n$ then the refractive index of the medium is _________.
(All given measurement are in SI units)
questions.sol:
Speed in the medium $v=\dfrac{\omega}{k}=\dfrac{2.0\times10^{15}}{10^7}=2\times10^8$ m/s.
$n=\dfrac cv=\dfrac{3\times10^8}{2\times10^8}=1.5$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: A plane wave after passing through prism remains as plane wave but passing through small pin hole may become spherical wave.
Statement II: The curvature of a spherical wave emerging from a slit will increase for increasing slit width.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I is true: a prism only deviates a plane wavefront, while a very small aperture acts as a point source of secondary wavelets (Huygens).
Statement II is false: a wider slit diffracts less, so the emerging front is flatter and its curvature decreases.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The magnitudes of power of a biconvex lens (refractive index 1.5) and that of a plano-concave lens (refractive index = 1.7) are same. If the curvature of plano-concave lens exactly matches with the curvature of back surface of the biconvex lens, then ratio of radius of curvature of front and back surface of the biconvex lens is_______.
questions.sol:
Biconvex: $|P|\propto0.5\left(\dfrac1{R_1}+\dfrac1{R_2}\right)$. Plano-concave with radius $R_2$: $|P|\propto\dfrac{0.7}{R_2}$.
Equal powers: $\dfrac{0.5}{R_1}=\dfrac{0.2}{R_2}$, so $R_1:R_2=5:2$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: An atom ${}^{8}_{3}X$ is bombarded by shower of fundamental particles and in 10 s this atom absorbed 10 electrons, 10 protons and 9 neutrons. The percentage growth in the surface area of the nucleons is recorded by:
questions.sol:
Electrons do not change the nucleus. Mass number: $8\to8+10+9=27$.
$R\propto A^{1/3}$: the radius goes from $2R_0$ to $3R_0$, so the surface area becomes $\left(\tfrac32\right)^2=2.25$ times the original, i.e. $225\%$ of it (the increase itself is $125\%$).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Assuming in forward bias condition there is a voltage drop of 0.7 V across a silicon diode, the current through diode $D_1$ in the circuit is ______mA.
(Assume all diodes in the given circuit are identical)
questions.sol:
$D_1$ and $D_3$ are forward biased and $D_2$ is reverse biased, so no current flows through $D_2$.
Current through $R_1$: $\dfrac{12-0.7}{300}\ \mathrm{A}=37.7$ mA, shared equally by the identical diodes $D_1$ and $D_3$.
Current through $D_1\approx18.8$ mA.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A convex lens of refractive index 1.5 and focal length $f=18$ cm is immersed in water. The difference in focal lengths of the given lens when it is in water and in air is $\alpha\times f$. The value of $\alpha$ is _____.
(refractive index of water = 4/3)
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{f_w}{f}=\dfrac{1.5-1}{\dfrac{1.5}{4/3}-1}=\dfrac{0.5}{0.125}=4$, so $f_w=4f$.
Difference $=4f-f=3f$, so $\alpha=3$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: The equivalent resistance between the points $A$ and $B$ in the following circuit is $\dfrac x5\ \Omega$. The value of $x$ is __________.
questions.sol:
Label the top junction M and the bottom junction N. Then A-M is $6\ \Omega$, A-N is $3\ \Omega$, M-B is $3\ \Omega$, N-B is $6\ \Omega$, and M-N is $3\ \Omega$ (an unbalanced bridge).
With $V_A=1$, $V_B=0$, the node equations are $5V_M-2V_N=1$ and $5V_N-2V_M=2$, giving $V_M=\tfrac37$, $V_N=\tfrac47$.
Current from A $=\dfrac{4/7}{6}+\dfrac{3/7}{3}=\dfrac{5}{21}$, so $R_{AB}=\dfrac{21}{5}\ \Omega$ and $x=21$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
The ratio of de Broglie wavelength of a deutron with kinetic energy $E$ to that of an alpha particle with kinetic energy $2E$, is $n:1$. The value of $n$ is ____.
(Assume mass of proton = mass of neutron) :
questions.sol:
$\lambda=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}$. With $m_d=2m$ and $m_\alpha=4m$:
$\dfrac{\lambda_d}{\lambda_\alpha}=\sqrt{\dfrac{m_\alpha K_\alpha}{m_dK_d}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{4m\cdot2E}{2m\cdot E}}=2$, so $n=2$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text: A solid sphere of radius 10 cm is rotating about an axis which is at a distance 15 cm from its centre. The radius of gyration about this axis is $\sqrt n$ cm. The value of $n$ is
questions.sol:
$I=\tfrac25MR^2+Md^2=M\left(\tfrac25\cdot100+225\right)=265M$ (cm$^2$).
$k^2=265$, so $n=265$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.text: The displacement of a particle, executing simple harmonic motion with time period $T$, is expressed as $x(t)=A\sin\omega t$, where $A$ is the amplitude. The maximum value of potential energy of this oscillator is found at $t=T/2\beta$. The value of $\beta$ is ______.
questions.sol:
Potential energy is greatest at the extreme position, first reached when $\omega t=\pi/2$, i.e. $t=T/4$.
$\dfrac{T}{2\beta}=\dfrac T4$ gives $\beta=2$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Which of the following point in Figure 2 most accurately represents the nodal surface as shown in Figure 1?
questions.sol:
A nodal surface is where $\psi$ changes sign, so $\psi=0$ there.
In Figure 2, $\psi_{2s}$ crosses zero at B, which corresponds to the spherical (radial) node of Figure 1.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The wave numbers of three spectral lines of H atom are considered. Identify the set of spectral lines belonging to Balmer series.
(R = Rydberg constant)
questions.sol:
Balmer series: $\bar\nu=R\left(\dfrac14-\dfrac1{n^2}\right)$, $n=3,4,5,\ldots$
$n=3$: $\dfrac{5R}{36}$; $n=4$: $\dfrac{3R}{16}$; $n=5$: $\dfrac{21R}{100}$. This is option (3).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The number of species among $\mathrm{BF_4^-}$, $\mathrm{SiF_4}$, $\mathrm{XeF_4}$ and $\mathrm{SF_4}$, that have unequal E$-$F bond lengths is two. Here, E is the central atom.
Statement II: Among $\mathrm{O_2^-}$, $\mathrm{O_2^{2-}}$, $\mathrm{F_2}$ and $\mathrm{O_2^+}$, $\mathrm{O_2^-}$ has the highest bond order.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I: $\mathrm{BF_4^-}$ and $\mathrm{SiF_4}$ (tetrahedral) and $\mathrm{XeF_4}$ (square planar) have equal bonds; only $\mathrm{SF_4}$ (see-saw, axial and equatorial bonds) has unequal bonds. One species, not two: false.
Statement II: bond orders are $\mathrm{O_2^-}$ 1.5, $\mathrm{O_2^{2-}}$ 1, $\mathrm{F_2}$ 1, $\mathrm{O_2^+}$ 2.5. $\mathrm{O_2^+}$ is highest: false.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
$20.0\ \mathrm{dm^3}$ of an ideal gas 'X' at 600 K and 0.5 MPa undergoes isothermal reversible expansion until pressure of the gas is 0.2 MPa. Which of the following option is correct?
(Given: log 2 = 0.3010 and log 5 = 0.6989)
questions.sol:
Isothermal ideal gas: $\Delta U=\Delta H=0$ and $q=-w$.
$w=-p_1V_1\ln\dfrac{p_1}{p_2}=-(0.5\times10^6)(20\times10^{-3})(2.303)\log2.5$.
$\log2.5=0.6989-0.3010=0.3979$, so $w=-10^4\times0.916\approx-9.1$ kJ and $q=+9.1$ kJ.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: At T(K), 2 moles of liquid A and 3 moles of liquid B are mixed. The vapour pressure of ideal solution formed is 320 mm Hg. At this stage, one mole of A and one mole of B are added to the solution. The vapour pressure is now measured as 328.6 mm Hg. The vapour pressure (in mm Hg) of A and B are respectively:
questions.sol:
Raoult's law: $\tfrac25p_A^0+\tfrac35p_B^0=320$, i.e. $2p_A^0+3p_B^0=1600$.
After the addition (3 mol A, 4 mol B): $\tfrac37p_A^0+\tfrac47p_B^0=328.6$, i.e. $3p_A^0+4p_B^0\approx2300$.
Solving: $p_B^0\approx200$ and $p_A^0=500$ mm Hg.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider a weak base 'B' of $\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{b}=5.699$. 'x' mL of 0.02 M HCl and 'y' mL of 0.02 M weak base 'B' are mixed to make 100 mL of a buffer of pH 9 at 25 $^\circ$C. The values of 'x' and 'y' respectively are:
[Given: log 2 = 0.3010, log 3 = 0.4771, log 5 = 0.699]
questions.sol:
pOH $=5=\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{b}+\log\dfrac{[\mathrm{BH^+}]}{[\mathrm B]}$, so $\log\dfrac{[\mathrm{BH^+}]}{[\mathrm B]}=-0.699$ and the ratio is $0.2$.
$[\mathrm{BH^+}]\propto x$ and $[\mathrm B]\propto y-x$: $\dfrac{x}{y-x}=0.2$, so $y=6x$.
With $x+y=100$: $x=14.3$ mL, $y=85.7$ mL.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
An organic compound undergoes first order decomposition. The time taken for decomposition to $\left(\dfrac18\right)^{\text{th}}$ and $\left(\dfrac1{10}\right)^{\text{th}}$ of its initial concentration are $t_{1/8}$ and $t_{1/10}$ respectively.
What is the value of $\dfrac{t_{1/8}}{t_{1/10}}\times10$ ?
(log 2= 0.3)
questions.sol:
For first order, $t=\dfrac{2.303}{k}\log\dfrac{[A]_0}{[A]}$.
$\dfrac{t_{1/8}}{t_{1/10}}=\dfrac{\log8}{\log10}=3(0.3)=0.9$; times 10 gives 9.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: In period 4 of the periodic table, the elements with highest and lowest atomic radii are respectively.
questions.sol:
Across a period the atomic radius decreases as the nuclear charge increases. In period 4 (K to Kr), the largest is K and, leaving out the noble gas, the smallest is Br.
Rb, Na and Cl are not in period 4.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text:
Regarding the hydrides of group 15 elements $\mathrm{EH_3}$ (E = N, P, As, Sb), select the correct statement from the following:
A. The stability of hydrides decreases down the group.
B. The basicity of hydrides decreases down the group.
C. The reducing character increases down the group.
D. The boiling point increases down the group.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
As the E$-$H bond weakens down the group, thermal stability falls and reducing character rises (A, C true). The lone pair becomes more diffuse, so basicity falls (B true).
Boiling point does not rise steadily: $\mathrm{NH_3}$ (hydrogen bonded) boils higher than $\mathrm{PH_3}$ and $\mathrm{AsH_3}$ (D false). Answer: A, B and C only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The correct statement among the following is:
options: $\mathrm{Ni(CO)_4}$ and $\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}$ are diamagnetic and $\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}}$ is paramagnetic.
$\mathrm{Ni(CO)_4}$ and $\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}}$ are diamagnetic and $\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}$ is paramagnetic.
$\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}$ and $\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}}$ are diamagnetic and $\mathrm{Ni(CO)_4}$ is paramagnetic.
$\mathrm{Ni(CO)_4}$ is diamagnetic and $\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}}$ and $\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}$ are paramagnetic.
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{Ni(CO)_4}$: Ni(0), $sp^3$ with $3d^{10}$, diamagnetic.
$\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}$: Ni(II) $3d^8$, strong-field $\mathrm{CN^-}$ pairs the electrons, $dsp^2$ square planar, diamagnetic.
$\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}}$: weak-field $\mathrm{Cl^-}$, $sp^3$ tetrahedral with two unpaired electrons, paramagnetic.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The number of pairs, from the following, in which both the ions are coloured in aqueous solution is 3.
$[\mathrm{Sc^{3+}, Ti^{3+}}]$, $[\mathrm{Mn^{2+}, Cr^{2+}}]$, $[\mathrm{Cu^{2+}, Zn^{2+}}]$ and $[\mathrm{Ni^{2+}, Ti^{4+}}]$
Statement II: $\mathrm{Th^{4+}}$ is the strongest reducing agent among $\mathrm{Th^{4+}}$, $\mathrm{Ce^{4+}}$, $\mathrm{Gd^{3+}}$ and $\mathrm{Eu^{2+}}$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I: $\mathrm{Sc^{3+}}$ ($3d^0$), $\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}$ ($3d^{10}$) and $\mathrm{Ti^{4+}}$ ($3d^0$) are colourless, so only $[\mathrm{Mn^{2+}, Cr^{2+}}]$ has both ions coloured: 1 pair, not 3. False.
Statement II: $\mathrm{Eu^{2+}}$ readily changes to the stable $+3$ state and is the strongest reducing agent; $\mathrm{Th^{4+}}$ (already $f^0$, stable $+4$) is not a reducing agent. False.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Method used for separation of mixture of products (B and C) obtained in the following reaction is
questions.note: The official final key gives fractional distillation. In practice the two isomers are also commonly separated by fractional crystallisation (their melting points differ widely), which is not among the options.
questions.sol:
Benzene with $\mathrm{Br_2/FeBr_3}$ gives bromobenzene (A); nitration then gives 1-bromo-2-nitrobenzene and 1-bromo-4-nitrobenzene (B and C).
The two isomers have fairly close boiling points (roughly $261\ ^\circ$C and $256\ ^\circ$C), so among the methods listed the final key takes fractional distillation, the method used when boiling points are close.
Neither isomer sublimes, and unlike o-nitrophenol neither is separated by steam distillation (no intramolecular hydrogen bonding).
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text:
CORRECT order of stability for the following is
$\mathrm{CH_2=CH^-}$, $\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2^-}$, $\mathrm{CH\equiv C^-}$
questions.sol:
A carbanion is more stable when the lone pair is in an orbital with more s character, as it is held closer to the nucleus.
sp ($\mathrm{HC\equiv C^-}$) $>$ sp$^2$ ($\mathrm{CH_2=CH^-}$) $>$ sp$^3$ ($\mathrm{CH_3CH_2^-}$).
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text:
$\mathrm{Ph-CH=CH_2\xrightarrow[\text{HBr}]{(\text{PhCOO})_2}}$ Product
Consider the above reaction
A. The reaction proceeds through a more stable radical intermediate.
B. The role of peroxide is to generate $\mathrm{H^\bullet}$ (Hydrogen radical).
C. During this reaction, benzene is formed as a byproduct.
D. 1$-$Bromo$-$2$-$phenylethane is formed as the minor product.
E. The same reaction in absence of peroxide proceeds via carbocation intermediate.
Identify the correct statements. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Peroxide effect: $(\mathrm{PhCOO})_2\to2\,\mathrm{PhCOO^\bullet}\to2\,\mathrm{Ph^\bullet}+2\,\mathrm{CO_2}$; $\mathrm{Ph^\bullet}+\mathrm{HBr}\to\mathrm{C_6H_6}+\mathrm{Br^\bullet}$. So benzene is a by-product (C true) and the peroxide generates $\mathrm{Br^\bullet}$, not $\mathrm{H^\bullet}$ (B false).
$\mathrm{Br^\bullet}$ adds to give the more stable benzylic radical (A true), so 1-bromo-2-phenylethane is the major product (D false).
Without peroxide, electrophilic addition goes through a carbocation (E true). Answer: A, C and E.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements for the following reaction sequence.
Statement I: Compound 'Z' will give yellow precipitate with NaOI.
Statement II: Compound 'Q' has two different types of 'H' atoms (aromatic : aliphatic) in the ratio 1:3.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{C_3H_6Cl_2}$ with excess $\mathrm{NaNH_2}$ (double dehydrohalogenation) gives propyne (Y).
Hydration ($\mathrm{Hg^{2+}}$, dil. $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$) gives acetone (Z), a methyl ketone, which gives yellow iodoform with NaOI: Statement I true.
Cyclic trimerisation in a red-hot iron tube gives mesitylene (Q, $\mathrm{C_9H_{12}}$): 3 aromatic H and 9 methyl H, ratio 1:3. Statement II true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the following reaction sequence
Compound (y) develops characteristic colour with neutral $\mathrm{FeCl_3}$ solution.
Identify the INCORRECT statement from the following for the above sequence.
options: Both compounds x and y will dissolve in NaOH.
Compound y will dissolve in $\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$ and evolve a gas.
Both compounds x and y will burn with sooty flame.
Compound x is more acidic than compound y.
questions.sol:
Molar mass $=2\times47=94$; C: $0.766\times94=72$ (6 C), H: $0.0638\times94=6$ (6 H), remainder 16 (1 O). So x is phenol, $\mathrm{C_6H_5OH}$.
Kolbe's reaction gives salicylic acid (y), which gives a violet colour with neutral $\mathrm{FeCl_3}$.
Salicylic acid is a carboxylic acid and is far more acidic than phenol, so statement (4) is incorrect; (2), (1) and (3) are correct.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are the four isomeric compounds (P, Q, R, S)
Identify correct statements from below.
A. Q, R and S will give precipitate with 2, 4 $-$ DNP.
B. P and Q will give positive Bayer's test.
C. Q and R will give sooty flame.
D. R and S will give yellow precipitate with $\mathrm{I_2/NaOH}$.
E. Q alone will deposit silver with Tollen's reagent
Choose the correct option.
options: A, B, D and E only
questions.sol:
P = 1-phenylprop-2-en-1-ol, Q = 3-phenylpropanal, R = 1-phenylpropan-2-one, S = 1-phenylpropan-1-one (all $\mathrm{C_9H_{10}O}$).
A: Q, R and S are carbonyl compounds and give 2,4-DNP derivatives (true). C: Q and R are aromatic and burn with a sooty flame (true). E: only the aldehyde Q reduces Tollens' reagent (true).
D: S is an ethyl ketone and does not give the iodoform test (false). So A, C and E.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Consider the following reactions giving major product. Identify the correct reaction.
questions.sol:
(3) Reduction of benzyl isocyanide gives the secondary amine $\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2NHCH_3}$, not benzylamine.
(4) Hoffmann bromamide degradation: $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CONH_2+Br_2+4KOH\to CH_3CH_2NH_2+2KBr+K_2CO_3+2H_2O}$. Correct.
(1) In benzanilide the ring attached to N is activated, so nitration occurs at its para position, not on the benzoyl ring.
(2) Aryl halides do not undergo the Gabriel phthalimide reaction.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
In the given pentapeptide, find out an essential amino acid (Y) and the sequence present in the pentapeptide:
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Reading from the $\mathrm{H_2N}$ end, the side chains are $\mathrm{CH(OH)CH_3}$ (threonine), $\mathrm{CH_2OH}$ (serine), $\mathrm{CH_2COOH}$ (aspartic acid), H (glycine) and $\mathrm{CH_3}$ (alanine).
Sequence: Thr$-$Ser$-$Asp$-$Gly$-$Ala. Of these, threonine is an essential amino acid.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Griss$-$Ilosvay test is used for the detection of nitrite ion, which involves the use of sulphanilic acid and $\alpha-$naphthylamine reagent.
Statement II: In the above test, sulphanilic acid is diazotized by the acidified nitrite ion, which on further coupling with $\alpha-$naphthylamine forms an azo$-$dye.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
In the Griess-Ilosvay test for nitrite, acidified nitrite diazotises sulphanilic acid, and the diazonium salt couples with $\alpha$-naphthylamine to give a red azo dye.
Both statements are true.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
X is the number of geometrical isomers exhibited by $\mathrm{[Pt(NH_3)(H_2O)BrCl]}$.
Y is the number of optically inactive isomer(s) exhibited by $\mathrm{[CrCl_2(ox)_2]^{3-}}$
Z is the number of geometrical isomers exhibited by $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_3(NO_2)_3]}$.
The value of X + Y + Z is ______.
questions.sol:
X: square planar [Mabcd] has 3 geometrical isomers.
Y: $\mathrm{[CrCl_2(ox)_2]^{3-}}$ has a trans form (optically inactive) and a cis form that exists as a pair of enantiomers (optically active). Y $=1$.
Z: $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_3(NO_2)_3]}$ has fac and mer isomers, Z $=2$.
X + Y + Z $=6$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
0.53 g of an organic compound (x) when heated with excess of nitric acid (concentrated) and then with silver nitrate gave 0.75 g of silver bromide precipitate. 1.0 g of (x) gave 1.32 g of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ gas on combustion. The percentage of hydrogen in the compound (x) is ____%. [Nearest Integer]
[Given: Molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ H : 1, C : 12, Br : 80, Ag : 108, O : 16 ; Compound (x) : $\mathrm{C_xH_yBr_z}$]
questions.sol:
%Br $=\dfrac{80}{188}\times\dfrac{0.75}{0.53}\times100=60.2\%$.
%C $=\dfrac{12}{44}\times\dfrac{1.32}{1.0}\times100=36.0\%$.
The compound contains only C, H and Br, so %H $=100-60.2-36.0=3.8\approx4$ (consistent with $\mathrm{C_4H_5Br}$).
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text: 500 mL of 1.2 M KI solution is mixed with 500 mL of 0.2 M $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ solution in basic medium. The liberated iodine was titrated with standard 0.1 M $\mathrm{Na_2S_2O_3}$ solution in the presence of starch indicator till the blue color disappeared. The volume (in L) of $\mathrm{Na_2S_2O_3}$ consumed is _____. (Nearest integer)
questions.sol:
In basic medium $\mathrm{MnO_4^-}$ is reduced to $\mathrm{MnO_2}$ (3 electrons each). $\mathrm{KMnO_4}=0.1$ mol accepts 0.3 mol of electrons; $\mathrm{KI}=0.6$ mol is in excess.
Iodine liberated $=0.15$ mol $\mathrm{I_2}$, which needs $2\times0.15=0.3$ mol $\mathrm{Na_2S_2O_3}$ ($\mathrm{I_2+2S_2O_3^{2-}\to2I^-+S_4O_6^{2-}}$).
Volume $=\dfrac{0.3}{0.1}=3$ L.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the following redox reaction taking place in acidic medium
$\mathrm{BH_4^-(aq)+ClO_3^-(aq)\longrightarrow H_2BO_3^-(aq)+Cl^-(aq)}$
If the Nernst equation for the above balanced reaction is
$\mathrm{E_{cell}=E^\circ_{cell}-\dfrac{RT}{nF}\ln Q}$,
then the value of n is _______ .(Nearest integer)
questions.sol:
In $\mathrm{BH_4^-}$ hydrogen is $-1$; in $\mathrm{H_2BO_3^-}$ it is $+1$ (B stays $+3$). Each $\mathrm{BH_4^-}$ loses $4\times2=8$ electrons.
Chlorine goes from $+5$ to $-1$: each $\mathrm{ClO_3^-}$ gains 6 electrons.
Balanced: $3\,\mathrm{BH_4^-}+4\,\mathrm{ClO_3^-}\to3\,\mathrm{H_2BO_3^-}+4\,\mathrm{Cl^-}+3\,\mathrm{H_2O}$, with $n=24$ electrons transferred.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the dissociation equilibrium of the following weak acid
$\mathrm{HA\rightleftharpoons H^+(aq)+A^-(aq)}$
If the pKa of the acid is 4, then the pH of 10 mM HA solution is _____ .(Nearest integer)
[Given: The degree of dissociation can be neglected with respect to unity]
questions.subject: Chemistry
